title: 2026 IPOs: Why Earnings Execution Trumps Listing Gains
description: Many investors who sold shares of top-performing 2026 IPOs on listing day actually booked losses. This trend highlights that short-term market sentiment often.

faq.q: Is it always bad to sell an IPO on listing day?
faq.a: Not always, but it often means you might miss out on significant long-term growth if the company is fundamentally strong. Selling on listing day is a speculative strategy aimed at quick profits, which carries its own risks.

faq.q: How can I assess an IPO's fundamentals?
faq.a: Look at the company's financial statements (revenue, profit, debt), management quality, competitive advantages, and the industry's growth prospects. The Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) is your primary source of information.

faq.q: What is the role of Grey Market Premium (GMP) in IPOs?
faq.a: GMP is an unofficial indicator of an IPO's demand in the parallel market before listing. While it can influence sentiment, it is not a reliable predictor of actual listing performance or long-term value and should be treated with caution.

faq.q: Are there tax implications for selling IPO shares?
faq.a: Yes, if you sell shares within 12 months of allotment, any profit is considered a short-term capital gain (STCG) and is taxed at 15% plus applicable surcharge and cess. If held for over 12 months, it's a long-term capital gain (LTCG), taxed at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year.

faq.q: Should I invest in every IPO that comes out?
faq.a: No, a selective approach is crucial. Only invest in companies that you understand, believe have strong fundamentals, and fit your investment strategy. Not all IPOs are good investments.

faq.q: What is a lock-in period for IPO shares?
faq.a: A lock-in period typically applies to promoter shares or shares allotted to anchor investors, restricting their sale for a certain duration (e.g., 6 months to 1 year) post-listing. This is to ensure commitment from key stakeholders. Retail investors usually do not have such lock-ins on their allotted shares.
